clue.text: Work on stage in Nunn drama (PS Mae goes west)

indicators.note: to go west is to be ruined or wrecked, so the letters of these words are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre director's production of a play, with a postscript noting that Mae West has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes west' looks like a nod to Mae West, but it is the anagram signal, applied to NUNN DRAMA PS MAE. Shaw's play is the work on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's comedy is a stage play, so it is a theatrical work.

clue.text: Printers moaned about Ruskin's work

indicators.note: about here means scattered around, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Typesetters complained about the work of a Victorian critic they had to print.
explanation.definitionFit: John Ruskin's multi-volume study of art criticism bore this title, so it is his work.

clue.text: Without name and rank, midwife is more agile

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so name and rank sit around the other piece

parts.note: a tier is a rank or row
read as mid-wife, the middle letters of the word wife

explanation.surface: A midwife who has shed her name and rank moves about more easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking; 'midwife' is read as mid-wife, the middle of the word wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Nifty means nimble or deft, and the comparative form means more nimble.

clue.text: Old type of wrought-iron panel

indicators.note: wrought means worked or shaped, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of an antique panel made of wrought iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrought' looks like part of 'wrought-iron' but it signals the anagram of IRON PANEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpareil was the name of an old printing type size, six points, used by printers.

clue.text: Prophet housing a distant traveller

indicators.note: housing means holding within, so the prophet's word contains the other pieces

parts.note: a seer is a prophet
far means distant

explanation.surface: A prophet gives shelter to a traveller from a faraway land.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor or voyager by sea is a kind of traveller.

clue.text: Rattle on the back burner

definitions.meaning: to rattle someone is to disconcert or unsettle them
something on the back burner has been postponed or deferred

explanation.surface: Someone flustered while a matter is left waiting on the stove.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to disconcert someone and, as a participle, postponed.

clue.text: Bound to make picture frame stick out

indicators.note: the stick is opened out to make room for letters placed inside it

parts.note: a rod is a stick

indicators.note: frame means the border, so only the first and last letters of picture are used

explanation.surface: Something is needed to make a picture frame stand out from the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frame' takes P and E, the first and last letters of 'picture', and these go inside ROD.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied with cords means bound, as a prisoner might be.

clue.text: With result assured everywhere, semiologist's starting his trip

parts.note: all over means everywhere
Roland Barthes was the French semiologist; the possessive 's gives the S

indicators.note: starting means the first letter of the word his is taken

parts.note: an outing is a trip

explanation.surface: A theorist of signs sets off on a journey, confident of how things will turn out everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Roland Barthes was a French literary theorist who studied signs, so the 's of 'semiologist's' supplies the S of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a contest whose outcome is settled, with only the cheering left to come.

clue.text: See 7
Object to article carried by skilful person in case

indicators.note: carried by means held within, so the skilful word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: deft means skilful
an end is an object or aim
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A skilled person in a legal case raises an objection to a newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skilful person' looks like one piece, but 'skilful' alone gives DEFT and 'person in case' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The accused party in a court case is the one who defends against the charge.

clue.text: Folk going round lake in island resort

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the folk word encloses the lake letter

parts.note: folks are one's parents, pa and ma
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Locals stroll round a lake at a holiday resort on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folk' in the sense of one's folks, the parents, gives PA and MA.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Majorca is a popular Mediterranean holiday destination on an island.

clue.text: A portion of okra — it apparently is served with an Indian meal

definitions.text: is served with an Indian meal

indicators.note: A portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A helping of okra is supposedly offered with a curry.
explanation.definitionFit: The yoghurt and cucumber side dish is a usual accompaniment to a curry in Indian cuisine.

clue.text: Instrument — a very loud one — with apparatus on deck

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
I is the Roman numeral for one
a davit is a small crane on a ship's deck for lowering boats

explanation.surface: A very loud musical instrument is played alongside equipment on a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests music, but here it is a legal instrument, a formal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A sworn written statement is a legal instrument, a formal document.

clue.text: Riddle, we hear, may be provided

indicators.note: we hear says the word is what something sounds like when spoken

parts.note: to riddle is to permeate throughout, to pervade

explanation.surface: A puzzle, it is said, might have been supplied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle, but it is the verb, as in 'riddled with': to pervade.
explanation.definitionFit: To purvey is to supply goods, so the past tense means supplied.

clue.text: Hard English novelist

parts.note: stern means hard or severe

explanation.surface: A severe English writer of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy, so he is a novelist.

clue.text: A ruler with a little boy outside getting ready to shoot

indicators.note: outside means placed around, so the boy's name encloses the other pieces

parts.note: Tim, as in Tiny Tim, the little boy in A Christmas Carol
a king is a ruler
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch and a small boy stand by as someone prepares to fire.
explanation.walkthrough: TIM is any boy's name, here Dickens's Tiny Tim.
explanation.definitionFit: Lining up a gun on a target is what one does when preparing to fire.

clue.text: Everyone is taken in by Plantagenet

indicators.note: taken in means placed inside, so the other pieces go into the word for by

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
all means everyone

explanation.surface: The whole court is fooled by a medieval English royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plantagenet' suggests the royal house, but it is Plantagenet Palliser, Trollope's politician in the Palliser novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Plantagenet is the first name of Trollope's character, Duke of Omnium, so the surname completes the name.

clue.text: Silly translation including Rimbaud's last poems

indicators.note: including means containing, so the rearranged letters hold the extra letter
translation turns the word into another form, so its letters are rearranged
last means the final letter of Rimbaud is taken

explanation.surface: A foolish rendering of the final verses of a French poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' makes IYLLS from SILLY, and 'including' puts D, the last letter of Rimbaud, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's Idylls of the King are short pastoral or narrative pieces of verse.

clue.text: We heard vowel sounds

indicators.note: heard says the words are what is spoken aloud

parts.note: the vowels U and I spoken, joined by and

explanation.surface: We listened to the noises of vowels.
explanation.walkthrough: Speak the letters U and I joined by 'and', and you hear the phrase for the pair of us.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the speaker plus the person addressed, which together make the plural pronoun.

clue.text: Reaction when left-leaning character loses heart

indicators.note: loses heart means the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: the backslash is a keyboard character that slopes to the left

explanation.surface: A reaction to a politician on the left who has become discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left-leaning character' suggests a socialist, but it is the typed symbol \ that leans left.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong adverse response against a trend or event is a reaction.

clue.text: Railing I have put under a vehicle?

indicators.note: in a down entry, put under means placed after, below the other piece

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person should be thrown under a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Railing' looks like a fence, but it is the present participle of rail, to rant.
explanation.definitionFit: Railing at someone is ranting with insults, which is verbally offensive behaviour.

clue.text: Dolly's a bit forward

parts.note: a part is a bit
on means forward, as in moving on

explanation.surface: A doll is a little too pushy.
explanation.walkthrough: Dolly is Dolly Parton, the American country singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolly is the first name of the country singer, so her surname completes it.

clue.text: Small image on Tom's collar?

parts.note: Tom Thumb, the tiny folk-tale hero
to collar or nail someone is to catch them

explanation.surface: A tiny picture printed on a cat's collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collar' is the verb, to arrest, and 'on' places one piece after the other in the across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A small preview version of a picture on a screen is a reduced image.

clue.text: Flourish with Orlando

definitions.meaning: to flourish is to thrive or blossom
Orlando ... is an English actor, and the setter's pseudonym is Orlando

explanation.surface: The setter signs off with a flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrive like a flower is to blossom, and the actor's surname is the same word.

clue.text: Uruguayan (a guy having emigrated) comes back from another country

indicators.note: comes back means the remaining letters are read in the reverse direction
having emigrated means these letters have left the word Uruguayan

explanation.surface: A South American, after a man leaves, returns from a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of A GUY (G, U, Y and the A after them) leave URUGUAYAN to give URUAN, then 'comes back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific island republic is a sovereign nation, a country distinct from Uruguay.

clue.text: Call round for drummer

parts.note: to ring is to call on the telephone
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A request to telephone a percussionist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer.

clue.text: Morrison accepts review — one written by conductor

indicators.note: accepts means taking in, so the name holds the other pieces

parts.note: Toni Morrison, the American novelist
to scan is to look over or review
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A novelist agrees to a critique of a book by a famous maestro.
explanation.walkthrough: Toni Morrison was the Nobel-winning American novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Composer providing big drummer with song

indicators.note: providing means furnishing new material, so the letters are made into something new

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A songwriter supplying a large percussionist with a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'providing' signals the anagram of BIG DRUMMER plus SONG; Sigmund Romberg wrote operettas such as The Student Prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigmund Romberg was a Hungarian-born American composer of operettas.
